candidate_relations.label: Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly states the patient was previously misdiagnosed with tenosynovial giant cell tumor by MRI. The fishbone penetration history, granulomatous reaction pattern, and clinical course point to a foreign body granuloma rather than a true neoplasm. TGCT is an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Neoplastic entity vs. reactive granulomatous process; was the prior misdiagnosis in this case

candidate_relations.label: Synovitis
candidate_relations.reason: Synovial hyperplasia and synovitis are documented findings on imaging and listed as preliminary diagnoses, but they represent the tissue reaction to the foreign body rather than the underlying diagnosis. Missing the etiology (foreign body/fishbone) and granulomatous nature.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Synovitis is a manifestation/component of the foreign body granuloma reaction, not the final diagnostic entity

candidate_relations.label: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath
candidate_relations.reason: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath is the localized form of TGCT, a neoplastic process. The reference diagnosis is a reactive foreign body granuloma triggered by a fishbone. These are distinct entities with incompatible etiologies, though both can involve the tendon sheath region.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Neoplastic localized form of TGCT vs. reactive foreign body granuloma; incompatible etiology and nature

candidate_relations.label: Foreign body-induced granuloma
candidate_relations.reason: Foreign body-induced granuloma is a direct semantic equivalent of 'foreign body granuloma.' The fishbone penetration history 6 months prior, chronic progressive tenosynovitis unresponsive to treatment, and imaging findings all support this diagnosis. The etiology (foreign body) and pathological process (granuloma) are both captured.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Foreign body granuloma with implied fishbone etiology; semantically equivalent to reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis 'Foreign body granuloma' is well-supported by the fishbone penetration history and clinical course, though histopathological confirmation is not explicitly documented in the record.
Prior misdiagnosis of TGCT is explicitly noted, making C001 and C003 clearly conflicting rather than uncertain.
